transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-12 15:00 PST | Duration: ~42 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Kapoor, Miguel Santos (Redwood) - Laura Chen, Tom Alvarez, Nina Patel, Evan Brooks (Acadia)

Summary auto-generated: We ran through the customer security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ style overlap), flagged controls that need evidence, and agreed next actions. Transcription quality medium — some acronyms mis-captured.

[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everybody, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan with Redwood Inference, AE on this account. We got Priya and Miguel from security and infra, and we'll walk through your vendor risk questionnaire and call out what we can provide as evidence.

[00:00:16] Laura Chen: Thanks Jordan. We're on a fairly compressed timeline, we've got the vendor risk intake due next Friday, and a procurement panel the following week. So trying to understand what artifacts you can provide — SOC 2, ISO, penetration test, that kind of thing.

[00:00:32] Priya Kapoor: Hi Laura, Nina, Tom — quick context: Redwood runs a unified inference platform with hosted, dedicated, and private options. For most SIG/CAIQ items we map to SOC 2 controls and we can provide a control matrix. We'll clarify what counts as evidence versus attestation.

[00:00:50] Tom Alvarez: Great. First question — data residency. Our policy mandates EU-only data residency for EU customers. How does Redwood handle region locking and backups?

[00:01:02] Miguel Santos: We support region-level tenancy. Hosted endpoints can be pinned to EU regions. Backups and blob storage options are region-aware; we can provide architecture diagram that shows region separation. Note: if you need physical on-prem or air-gapped, we have a Private deployment option but that is a separate contract.

[00:01:22] Nina Patel: And for the SOC 2 report — you said you can share a Type II. Is it redacted or full? We need to ingest into our VRM portal.

[00:01:33] Jordan Lee: We typically share the SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA/secure share. It can be redacted but we also provide a control mapping spreadsheet that maps SIG/CAIQ items to SOC 2 controls and evidence artifacts. I'll upload the report to a secure portal link.

[00:01:48] Laura Chen: On CAIQ — do you have an answered CAIQ spreadsheet or do we need to map?

[00:01:54] Priya Kapoor: We maintain a CAIQ/consensus spreadsheet. We'll attach our answers, and where we rely on underlying cloud provider controls we annotate that. There may be a few items that require supporting docs like penetration test reports or config screenshots.

[00:02:08] Tom Alvarez: Speaking of pen test — do you do annual pen tests and share a summary / remediation plan?

[00:02:14] Miguel Santos: Yes, we do third-party pen tests annually. We can provide the executive summary and remediation attestations. Full reports sometimes contain customer-identifiable details so we handle those on a case-by-case basis.

[00:02:30] Evan Brooks: For authentication — our requirement is SAML 2.0 with IdP-initiated SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Can Redwood integrate with Okta and enforce RBAC groups?

[00:02:41] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely. We support SAML 2.0 IdP and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based with least privilege defaults; we can show the role mapping sample and SCIM attribute mapping. If you need group syncing and comanaged provisioning we can share config snippets.

[00:02:58] Laura Chen: Audit logs are critical for us. We need logs for admin activity, config changes, model deployments, API keys usage, and all admin console activity. What's your retention and access model?

[00:03:12] Miguel Santos: Default logs are kept for 90 days in hosted environment. For Dedicated/Private and enterprise add-on we can extend to 13 months or custom retention, and export logs to your SIEM via secure syslog/Kinesis/S3 forwarder. We can provide a redacted 30-day sample showing admin events, token issuance, and model artifact changes.

[00:03:31] Tom Alvarez: When you say "redacted", what fields get redacted? We can't accept logs that include customer PII or raw prompt content.

[00:03:39] Priya Kapoor: Correct — by default we redact prompt/response content in shared samples. We can include metadata like request IDs, timestamps, account IDs (pseudonymized), and action types. For full forensic access you would request a dedicated export under legal/contract terms and we can provide it via secure transfer.

[00:03:57] Nina Patel: KMS — we need customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. Is CMK supported?

[00:04:03] Miguel Santos: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) in Dedicated and Private deployments and in Hosted for enterprise customers via envelope encryption with your KMS in the same region (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). We also support HSM-backed keys on request. We'll include the KMS integration guide as part of artifacts.

[00:04:20] Jordan Lee: I'm going to note as an action item: provide the KMS integration docs and the specific API call patterns used for envelope encryption.

[00:04:27] Laura Chen: Auditability/traceability: do you log key usage (e.g., CMK decrypt calls) for customer-managed keys?

[00:04:33] Miguel Santos: KMS provider will log key usage (CloudTrail for AWS KMS). We capture pointer events in our audit logs that show when keys were used for model encryption operations, but the actual key usage record lives in the customer's KMS audit logs. We'll document how to correlate ours with your KMS logs.

[00:04:50] Tom Alvarez: Incident response — what's your SLA to notify customers for security incidents and do you have an IR runbook?

[00:04:57] Priya Kapoor: We have an incident response policy and playbooks; notification timelines are in our security policy—critical incidents are notified within 24 hours. We'll provide the IR summary and stat report. For enterprise contracts we can include specific notification SLAs.

[00:05:12] Laura Chen: On the CAIQ, we have several control families flagged: identity mgmt, data protection, logging & monitoring, third-party mgmt. Can you walk us through the answers for identity mgmt quickly?

[00:05:22] Priya Kapoor: Sure. Identity mgmt — we integrate SAML SSO, support SCIM provisioning, enforce MFA for console access, and support RBAC to scope permissions. For service-to-service we use short-lived mTLS tokens and rotate keys automatically. We'll point you to the configuration page in our docs and show sample policies.

[00:05:40] Tom Alvarez: You mentioned mTLS for internal tokens — can you expand? We require mutual auth for upstream model servers when deployed in Dedicated clusters.

[00:05:47] Miguel Santos: For Dedicated clusters we enable mutual TLS between internal service mesh endpoints. Certificates are rotated via our cert manager and can be signed by your CA if required. We'll include cert rotation cadence and sample Kubernetes secret manifests for Private deployment.

[00:06:05] Nina Patel: Compliance certifications — do you have ISO 27001 or equivalents?

[00:06:10] Jordan Lee: We are ISO 27001 certified — I'll include the cert and scope. We also maintain SOC 2 Type II and can provide a summary of the scope, boundaries, and excluded components.

[00:06:21] Laura Chen: Where do you store backups and what's the retention policy for backups? Also are backups encrypted with the same KMS?

[00:06:30] Miguel Santos: Backups are stored in region-local encrypted buckets and use envelope encryption with either our service-managed keys or your CMK depending on contract. Standard retention is 30 days for ephemeral backups, long-term snapshots can be configured per-customer. We'll include the backup architecture diagram in the artifacts.

[00:06:46] Tom Alvarez: Regarding vendor risk questionnaire logistics — we need evidence attachments for a handful of questions. What's the preferred mechanism to receive these files? Our VRM system accepts secure links or direct upload.

[00:06:57] Jordan Lee: We can provide an SSO-protected secure share or deliver via your vendor portal. Common pattern: we upload SOC2, CAIQ spreadsheet, ISO certs, pen test exec summary to a secure share and send you a link. For anything more sensitive like raw logs, we open a ticket and use an encrypted transfer.

[00:07:14] Laura Chen: Good. On the CAIQ there's an item about privileged access reviews — how do you handle admin access reviews and periodic attestations?

[00:07:22] Priya Kapoor: We enforce review cadence — admin accounts are reviewed quarterly in our access control system, and we can provide attestation reports that show changes and approvals. We also provide admin change logs that show who granted what role when.

[00:07:34] Tom Alvarez: Any multi-tenant data separation concerns? We need assurance that customer A cannot access customer B data or keys.

[00:07:42] Miguel Santos: Multi-tenancy is logical — strong isolation at the tenancy layer, namespace-level KV caches, and encryption keys scoped per-customer. For Dedicated and Private you get physical or network segmentation. We'll provide tenancy design docs and evidence around logical separation controls.

[00:07:55] Nina Patel: A couple of specific VRM items flagged for evidence: 1) vulnerability management — patching cadence, 2) disaster recovery RTO/RPO, 3) vendor subprocessor list and contracts. Can you provide those?

[00:08:07] Priya Kapoor: Yes. Vulnerability mgmt: weekly scanning and monthly patch cadence for base images, emergency patches as required. DR: typical RTO is 4 hours for critical services, RPO depends on customer profile — we will include the DR summary. Subprocessor list: we'll attach current subprocessor list and data processing addendum.

[00:08:23] Laura Chen: There's a question about business continuity and whether you conduct tabletop exercises — provide evidence?

[00:08:29] Miguel Santos: We run annual tabletop exercises; can provide summary after-action reports without customer-sensitive details.

[00:08:36] Tom Alvarez: For the CAIQ matrix, can you pre-fill where you have cloud provider responsibility? We want to reduce back-and-forth.

[00:08:44] Priya Kapoor: We'll pre-fill and annotate shared-responsibility items. We'll flag items that require configuration on Acadia's side and mark required attestation.

[00:08:54] Jordan Lee: I'll ask for the specific VRM IDs from Laura so we can map them directly to our control matrix.

[00:09:00] Laura Chen: Sure. We'll send over the VRM export after the call.

[00:09:05] Nina Patel: Quick question — do you maintain a change management log for model updates (model rollouts, quantization changes, prompt templates)? We need to know who approved model changes.

[00:09:15] Priya Kapoor: Yes — model lifecycle events are recorded in our artifact registry. We log version, who triggered the rollout, the change reason, QA pass/fail notes, and can export a change history for a given model ID.

[00:09:29] Evan Brooks: How do you handle data retention for embeddings and cached KV? We can't have persistent embeddings of PII.

[00:09:37] Miguel Santos: We have configurable caching and TTLs: default short-lived KV caches for prompts, and optional longer-term embeddings persistence only if customer opts in and consents. For PII we recommend disabling persistence or routing to Dedicated with controlled storage. We'll include recommended configuration.

[00:09:55] Tom Alvarez: Any green flags from a security perspective that we should note in the VRM?

[00:10:01] Priya Kapoor: Some positives — SOC2 & ISO certifications, customer-managed KMS option, fine-grained RBAC & SAML/SCIM support, and the ability to export logs to your SIEM. We'll call those out in our cover note.

[00:10:12] Laura Chen: For the evidence pipeline: when you upload docs, do you timestamp and checksum the artifacts so we can verify integrity?

[00:10:19] Miguel Santos: Yes, artifacts uploaded to the secure share have checksums and we can provide SHA256 checksums on request.

[00:10:26] Jordan Lee: Ok, logistics aside — anything blocking us from providing the core artifacts this week?

[00:10:31] Laura Chen: Not blocking, just timing. We'll need the SOC2 and CAIQ answers by Friday to meet our internal review.

[00:10:38] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll prioritize.

[00:10:41] Priya Kapoor: One more technical note on logging: request/response bodies are not stored in audit logs by default in hosted; we store metadata and hashed identifiers. For customers that require request reconstruction we offer a controlled forensics export under contract.

[00:11:00] Tom Alvarez: About keys again — if we bring our own KMS, who holds responsibility for key rotation and compromise?

[00:11:08] Miguel Santos: If you supply CMKs, you control the lifecycle and rotation policy; Redwood will call KMS APIs as required but we don't have access to raw key material. Responsibility splits are defined in the DPA. We'll provide the DPA and key responsibilities clause.

[00:11:22] Nina Patel: Can you show an example of the audit log events that indicate role changes — like an admin granting a new role?

[00:11:28] Priya Kapoor: We'll extract a redacted snippet showing event type, timestamp, acting principal (pseudonymized), target principal, and change reason. That will be part of the logs sample.

[00:11:42] Evan Brooks: For private deployment: do you ship a deployable artifact or a managed appliance? We need to know network requirements and firewall ports.

[00:11:50] Miguel Santos: Private comes as a deployable package with a control plane that can be customer-hosted. We'll include an install checklist, ports diagram, and minimum compute requirements. For air-gapped installs we have an offline bundle process.

[00:12:04] Tom Alvarez: Are there any known limitations or 'exceptions' commonly called out in VRMs that we should flag early?

[00:12:11] Priya Kapoor: Common exceptions: request/response storage policies (we default to not storing request bodies), need-for-legal-to-release full log data, and provider-managed backups for short retention. We can pre-accept some exceptions in contract if needed.

[00:12:26] Laura Chen: How will you annotate CAIQ items that are delegated to CSP (cloud provider)?

[00:12:31] Priya Kapoor: We'll annotate each item and include references to the cloud provider's public compliance artifacts (e.g., AWS Artifact). We will notate responsibilities for the control as Redwood-owned, provider-owned, or shared.

[00:12:44] Jordan Lee: For next steps I'll: 1) upload SOC2 and CAIQ, 2) send the architecture diagram and KMS guide, 3) open a VT ticket for logs, 4) set up follow-up meeting for CAIQ deep dive. Anything to add?

[00:12:58] Laura Chen: Please also include pen test executive summary and subprocessor list.

[00:13:04] Jordan Lee: Will do.

[00:13:08] Priya Kapoor: We'll pre-fill the CAIQ spreadsheet and send it with annotations. If Tom wants a technical deep dive we can schedule a separate session with Infra and SEs to demo the audit export.

[00:13:20] Tom Alvarez: That'd be helpful — schedule for next week if possible.

[00:13:25] Jordan Lee: I'll propose a few times.

[00:13:28] Nina Patel: One last question from procurement — pricing and contract redlines: are there standard clauses for security incidents and liability?

[00:13:36] Jordan Lee: We have standard enterprise terms; for security incidents we include notification SLAs and cooperation clauses. For specific liability caps we can discuss with legal — I'll connect you to our Contracts lead.

[00:13:47] Laura Chen: Thanks — this was a good walkthrough. We'll send the VRM export and expect the artifacts.

[00:13:53] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks everyone. We'll upload the items and follow up.

[00:14:00] [END RECORDING]

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-heard acronyms ("SOC two" vs "SOC 2"), and stutters that were not removed. Artifacts promised: SOC2 Type II, CAIQ answers, ISO cert, pen test exec summary, architecture diagram, KMS integration guide, redacted audit logs sample, subprocessor list, DPA and DR summary.
